title: Scheme robustness of the cutoff
text: The stretched singularity is robust at order one against the choice of Planck criterion: the curvature-eigenvalue condition $2M/r^3 = 1$, the Kretschmann condition $48M^2/r^6 = 1$, and the unit-proper-time condition $\tau(r) = 1$ (with $\tau = \tfrac23 r^{3/2}(2M)^{-1/2}(1 + O(r/2M))$ the proper time to the singularity) all yield $r_c = c_0\,M^{1/3}\lP^{2/3}$ with order-one constants: $c_0 = 2^{1/3}$, $48^{1/6}$, and $(3/2)^{2/3}\,2^{1/3}$ respectively. The surface where the algebra requires completion is, at this order, unambiguous.
proof: Each condition is solved exactly for $r$. Curvature eigenvalue: $r^3 = 2M$, so $r_c = (2M)^{1/3} = 2^{1/3}M^{1/3}$. Kretschmann: $r^6 = 48M^2$, so $r_c = 48^{1/6}M^{1/3}$. Proper time: from the exact interior integral $\tau(r) = \int_0^r \sqrt{u/(2M - u)}\,du = \tfrac{2}{3}\,r^{3/2}(2M)^{-1/2}(1 + O(r/2M))$ (the leading term of the series proved in \cite[Lem.~5.1]{ButlerT6} (\claimref{interior.kasner-form-interior}), rescaled to $2M \neq 1$), setting $\tau = 1$ gives $r_c = (3/2)^{2/3}(2M)^{1/3}(1 + O(r_c/M))$. All three are $M^{1/3}$ times constants $2^{1/3} \approx 1.26$, $48^{1/6} \approx 1.91$, $(3/2)^{2/3}2^{1/3} \approx 1.65$: order one. The script checks the three exponent computations and the constants exactly (as exact powers of rationals).

4\pi\,r_c^2\,\sqrt{2M/r_c} \;=\; 4\pi\,\sqrt{2M}\;r_c^{3/2} \;=\; 4\pi\,\sqrt{2M}\,\sqrt{2M} \;=\; 8\pi M

title: The clock inventory of the boundary modes
proof: (i) is the algebra's own inventory: a one-parameter group of inner automorphisms of a Clifford algebra preserving the vector grade is generated by an even element whose commutator preserves grade one, i.e.\ by a bivector (the commutator of a vector with a grade-$2k$ element has grade $2k - 1$, so only $k = 1$ preserves the vector space; a mixed even generator $A_2 + A_4 + \cdots$ reduces to its bivector part, since grade preservation forces $[A_{2k}, v] = 0$ for every vector $v$ when $k \geq 2$, making each higher $A_{2k}$ central, and an even central element is a scalar; scalars generate nothing). The single-pair clause of (ii) is the import, proved in \cite[Prop.~2.1]{ButlerT7} (\claimref{hawking.modular-structure-completed-pair}), unique up to reparametrisation and orientation: the algebra fixes the orbits, not the speed, and the geometric normalisation of \cite[App.~A]{ButlerT5} is what fixes the speed, converting rapidity, and only rapidity, to Schwarzschild time at $\kappa = 1/4M$, so a rescaled generator traverses the same orbits and defines the same clock, not a faster one. For (iii): the flow a bivector $X$ generates acts on the mode operators by $\operatorname{ad}_X$, which is insensitive to a central shift ($\operatorname{ad}_{E_{ii}} = \operatorname{ad}_{E_{ii} - 1/2}$), so it is the adjoint spectrum and not the one-particle spectrum that the classification must read. From the canonical anticommutation relations of the mode operators (Proposition \claimref{scrambling.boundary-mode-space-matrix}), $[E_{ij}, \psi_k^\dagger] = \delta_{jk}\psi_i^\dagger$ and $[E_{ij}, \psi_k] = -\delta_{ik}\psi_j$. Hence $\operatorname{ad}_{E_{ii}}$ has eigenvalues $\pm 1$ on $(\psi_i^\dagger, \psi_i)$ and $0$ elsewhere, and the atom's boost bivector $\sigma_i = 2(\hat n_i - \tfrac12)$ (Fact \claimref{scrambling.imported-modes-modular-inventory}) generates that same flow in the rotor convention $e^{\sigma_i t/2}(\cdot)\,e^{-\sigma_i t/2}$: unit rapidity. The equal-coefficient sum $\sum_i E_{ii}$ gives $\pm 1$ on every mode, the simultaneous boost of all $n$ atoms and the statement's common clock; what is compact here is the phase circle $e^{i\theta \hat n}$, whose generator is $i$ times a bivector, which the real Clifford algebra of the boundary modes excludes, its centre being scalar, so the phase circle is not an intrinsic flow in the sense of (i); the single-atom instance of the exclusion is published as \cite[Prop.~7.21(3)]{ButlerT5} (\claimref{singularity.euclidean-rotor-where-it-lies}). For $i \neq j$, $\operatorname{ad}_{E_{ij} + E_{ji}}$ has eigenvectors $\psi_i^\dagger \pm \psi_j^\dagger$ with eigenvalues $\pm 1$, and $E_{ij} + E_{ji} = \hat n_+ - \hat n_-$ exactly in the rotated modes $(\psi_i \pm \psi_j)/\sqrt{2}$: again unit rapidity. The antisymmetric $E_{ij} - E_{ji}$ has adjoint eigenvalues $\pm i$ and is compact; the single $E_{ij}$ with $i \neq j$ is nilpotent, generating a unipotent shear; neither carries a rapidity. A diagonal $\sum_i c_i E_{ii}$ has adjoint eigenvalues $\pm c_i$, so unequal $|c_i|$ leave no common rapidity and admit no single conversion. The pairing sector is classified by one product: from the CAR, $\operatorname{ad}$ of $c\,\psi_i^\dagger\psi_j^\dagger + d\,\psi_j\psi_i$ maps $\psi_i^\dagger \mapsto d\,\psi_j$, $\psi_j \mapsto c\,\psi_i^\dagger$, $\psi_j^\dagger \mapsto -d\,\psi_i$, $\psi_i \mapsto -c\,\psi_j^\dagger$, two $2 \times 2$ blocks each with eigenvalues $\pm\sqrt{cd}$: hyperbolic for $cd > 0$, where unequal coefficients rescale the common rapidity rather than remove it ($2\psi_i^\dagger\psi_j^\dagger + \tfrac12\psi_j\psi_i$ is a clock at unit rapidity outright); compact for $cd < 0$, eigenvalues $\pm i\sqrt{|cd|}$; nilpotent for $cd = 0$. Every clock in the inventory is therefore hyperbolic with unit rapidity after normalisation, hence by the Witt-extension clause of (iii), in the split space of the $n$ hyperbolic pairs of \claimref{tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity}, $O(n,n)$-conjugate to a sum of standard atom boosts, and the geometric normalisation converts them all at the one $\kappa$. What is unique is the rate, not the flow. Normalisation sets the nonzero adjoint eigenvalues to $\pm 1$, so the continuation of any clock to imaginary rapidity acts on the mode operators by $e^{\pm i\theta}$ and has conjugation period exactly $2\pi$, the atom's period of Fact \claimref{scrambling.imported-modes-modular-inventory} (\cite[Prop.~7.21(1)]{ButlerT5}); at the geometric rate $\kappa$ that period is the Schwarzschild span $2\pi/\kappa = \beta$.

title: The epoch is the modular period; two unknowns become one
text:
Assume (IC). Then the counted epoch is the modular period:
\[
\Delta t \;=\; \beta \;=\; \frac{2\pi}{\kappa} \;=\; 8\pi M \qquad \text{(Schwarzschild)}.
\]
The conversion is exact and holds in both directions: with the epoch fixed, the area-law condition $\nu\,\Delta t = M/2$ of Proposition \claimref{scrambling.area-law-test} becomes a prediction for the density factor,
\[
\nu \;=\; \frac{M/2}{8\pi M} \;=\; \frac{1}{16\pi}
\]
in the 1-nat convention ($\nu = 1/(16\pi\ln 2)$ in T5's capacity convention, Remark \claimref{note.scrambling.density-factor-stated-full}; the section ``The calibration factorised, and the quarter examined'' shows the capacity convention is the one with physical content and restates the prediction there), and a calibration principle for the exceptional set (Fact \claimref{tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity}; the section ``The calibration factorised, and the quarter examined'' says what it must produce) must return that number \emph{or refute the premise (IC)}. Two unknowns have become one equation and one falsifiable identification; the count's remaining condition is a single dimensionless number with a named derivation route and a named failure mode. The scale $\Delta t \sim M$ is thereby derived rather than imported, cohering with Theorem \claimref{scrambling.mode-count}'s own observation that the accrual rate is set by the horizon's temperature: the singularity keeps the horizon's scale.
proof: By Lemma \claimref{scrambling.clock-inventory-boundary-modes} every clock of the boundary modes runs at the modular rate $\kappa$, with period $\beta = 8\pi M$: the flows differ, the rate does not. (IC, \claimref{scrambling.intrinsic-clock-ic-flagged-premise}) says the epoch is set by an intrinsic clock, and a clock marks a span through its period: a hyperbolic flow has exactly one, the $2\pi$ conjugation cycle of its Euclidean continuation: a clock is $O(n,n)$-conjugate to a sum of standard atom boosts (Lemma \claimref{scrambling.clock-inventory-boundary-modes}), the atom's cycle is \cite[Prop.~7.21(1)]{ButlerT5} (\claimref{singularity.euclidean-rotor-where-it-lies}), and the geometric normalisation converts it to $2\pi/\kappa = \beta$, whereas the e-folding time $\kappa^{-1}$ is rapidity one and closes no cycle. Every candidate clock carries the same period, so $\Delta t = \beta$. The displayed conversion is arithmetic, verified exactly by the script; the two-direction clause is Proposition \claimref{scrambling.area-law-test} read in each direction.

title: The integer-holographic form, and the identification of the $16\pi$
proof: All three clauses are exact arithmetic from Theorem \claimref{scrambling.mode-count} and Theorem \claimref{scrambling.epoch-modular-period-two-unknowns-become}: $V = 8\pi M \cdot 8\pi M = 64\pi^2 M^2$ and $\beta^2 = (8\pi M)^2$; $\nu V = 64\pi^2M^2/16\pi = 4\pi M^2$; and $V/\SBH = 64\pi^2M^2/4\pi M^2 = 16\pi = A/M^2$. The script checks each as an exact identity in the formal symbols $(\pi, M)$.

title: The circularity fence
text: T5's capacity statement (the Page-curve computation) \emph{cites} the count of the section ``The count'' and the area-law condition under test; any derivation of the epoch routed through the Page-curve or eviction computation therefore proves the prediction from itself, and is excluded. Admissible derivations of $\nu = 1/16\pi$ in the 1-nat convention, $\nu = 1/(16\pi\ln 2)$ in the capacity convention (Remark \claimref{note.scrambling.density-factor-stated-full}), must come from the structure of the boundary modes themselves (a calibration principle on the exceptional set of the weighted completion, the section ``The calibration factorised, and the quarter examined'', or the slice-to-epoch aggregation of the section ``The transverse sphere from the boundary modes''); the fence is part of what makes the prediction falsifiable, and the failed direct aggregations recorded in the section ``The transverse sphere from the boundary modes'' show that it excludes real candidates.

title: Point of contact: what kind of statement this is
text: The step of Theorem \claimref{scrambling.epoch-modular-period-two-unknowns-become} is the framework's version of a familiar holographic practice: when a quantity is conditional on a regulator, derive the regulator from the system's own modular structure. The coherence checks are threefold: the causal epoch of Fact \claimref{singularity.causal-epoch-computed-exactly} is $O(M)$ with an identified logarithm, matching the modular period's scale; the count's rate is set by the horizon's own temperature, $dN/dt = \nu/\TH$; and the epoch three-volume comes out as $\beta^2\lP$, modular up to a single Planck factor. None of the three is a proof of (IC), and the third is the weakest, its power of $\lP$ the residue of geometry; together they are why the premise is worth flagging rather than discarding.

title: The calibration factorised, and the quarter examined
text: Theorem \claimref{scrambling.epoch-modular-period-two-unknowns-become} leaves one number, and Fact \claimref{tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity} places it at the exceptional set of the weighted completion. The geometry paper's weighted limit holds at transport level along every tangential curve of fixed Hubble-normalised length for the whole admissible class (the metrics of \cite[Def.~5.5]{ButlerT6}, whose Kasner-type exponents satisfy $\sum_i p_i^2 = 1$, as Schwarzschild's $(-\tfrac13, \tfrac23, \tfrac23)$ do), and at Schwarzschild the $\varphi$-lines converge with rate $\tau^{1/3}$ and the boundary data are regular by symmetry \cite[\S 5.5]{ButlerT6}; the prediction is stated at Schwarzschild, where no billiard arises. So no analytic obstacle remains between the framework and $\nu$; what remains is a calibration principle, carried by this paper (Remark \claimref{note.scrambling.density-factor-stated-full}), and the results below say what it must produce: the required thinning factorises; exactness excludes the cutoff from the count and narrows the normalisation to two cutoff-free scales, the horizon $r_h$ and $r_* = M$; one tick per modular period is (IC) read as a counting rule; and the residue is Bekenstein-Hawking's quarter, which in the one convention that compares an entropy with an entropy is $1/(4\ln 2)$, unreachable by any counting rule whose residue is rational ($k = 0$ in Proposition \claimref{scrambling.no-recount-reaches-quarter}) and, conditionally on the expected algebraic independence of $\pi$ and $\ln 2$, by any counting rule at all.

title: Imported: the collar's coframe at the exceptional set, and the helicity lift
text: In units $2M = 1$ the weighted coframe of the Schwarzschild interior gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), the components of its physical-vector map $\hb^{-1}$ in the orthonormal frame adapted to $(t, \theta, \varphi)$, rescaled, carries the weights $r^{1/2}$ on $\sqrt{A}\,dt$ and $r^{-1}$ on $r\,d\theta$, $r\sin\theta\,d\varphi$: these are the Kasner exponents $(-\tfrac13, \tfrac23, \tfrac23)$ of the proper-time variable $\tau \propto r^{3/2}$ rewritten in the variable $r$, where they read $(-\tfrac12, 1, 1)$, normalised to one at $r = r_h$; the horizon-normalised coframe on the exceptional set is therefore $(dt,\ r_h\,d\theta,\ r_h\sin\theta\,d\varphi)$ exactly, $(r^{1/2}\sqrt{A})^2 = 1 - r \to 1$ and $r^{-1}\cdot r = 1$. In the Hawking paper's lift, each channel $(\omega, \ell, m, s)$ of the near-horizon reduction is one two-dimensional mode, and the two helicities of a massless species are two channels at distinct homogeneities $-2s - 2$ ($-4$ and $0$ for the photon, $-6$ and $+2$ for the graviton); the channel identification is that paper's joint J3, its one modelling joint, which it assigns to this paper as an open successor problem, so the lift enters here at modelling tier and not at theorem tier. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Lemmas 5.1 to 5.3, Def.~5.5]{ButlerT6} and \cite[Thm.~8.16]{ButlerT4} for the weights; \cite[Fact~5.1, Prop.~5.2, Assembly~5.3]{ButlerT7} for the lift, Assembly 5.3 there itemising J3 as modelling.
proof: The coframe below is that of the derived metric of the Schwarzschild interior gravitational field, the components of $\hb^{-1}$ in an orthonormal frame (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}(i)). In units $2M = 1$ the weighted coframe of the Schwarzschild interior carries the weights $r^{1/2}$ on $\sqrt{A}\,dt$ and $r^{-1}$ on $r\,d\theta$, $r\sin\theta\,d\varphi$: these are the Kasner exponents $(-\tfrac13, \tfrac23, \tfrac23)$ of the proper-time variable $\tau \propto r^{3/2}$ rewritten in the variable $r$, where they read $(-\tfrac12, 1, 1)$, normalised to one at $r = r_h$; the horizon-normalised coframe on the exceptional set is therefore $(dt,\ r_h\,d\theta,\ r_h\sin\theta\,d\varphi)$ exactly, $(r^{1/2}\sqrt{A})^2 = 1 - r \to 1$ and $r^{-1}\cdot r = 1$. In the Hawking paper's lift, each channel $(\omega, \ell, m, s)$ of the near-horizon reduction is one two-dimensional mode, and the two helicities of a massless species are two channels at distinct homogeneities $-2s - 2$ ($-4$ and $0$ for the photon, $-6$ and $+2$ for the graviton); the channel identification is that paper's joint J3, its one modelling joint, which it assigns to this paper as an open successor problem, so the lift enters here at modelling tier and not at theorem tier. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Lemmas 5.1 to 5.3, Def.~5.5]{ButlerT6} (\claimref{interior.interior-connection-exactly}, \claimref{interior.kasner-form-interior}) and \cite[Thm.~8.16]{ButlerT4} (\claimref{sheaf.weights-are-forced-are-kasner-exponents}) for the weights; \cite[Fact~5.1, Prop.~5.2, Assembly~5.3]{ButlerT7} (\claimref{hawking.homogeneity-ordering-shift}, \claimref{hawking.imported-penrose-transform}, \claimref{hawking.helicity-lift-joints-itemised}) for the lift, Assembly 5.3 there itemising J3 as modelling.

title: The exact factorisation of the thinning
proof: (i) and (ii) are Proposition \claimref{scrambling.slice-volume-exactly-per-unit-killing} and Theorem \claimref{scrambling.epoch-modular-period-two-unknowns-become}'s numbers multiplied, and inherit Proposition \claimref{scrambling.slice-volume-exactly-per-unit-killing}'s leading-order qualifier, the neglected factor being $\sqrt{1 - r_c/2M}$; (iii) is arithmetic, exact, $\beta/r_h = 8\pi M/2M = 4\pi$ and $A/\SBH = 4$. The script performs all of it as exact monomials in $\pi$ and $M$.

title: The calibration factorised, and the quarter examined
text: The two factors are different kinds of question. The $4\pi = \beta/r_h$ measures the modular period in units of the horizon's own Killing time scale; it is what disappears if the $t$-direction of the exceptional set is counted \emph{once per modular period} instead of once per slice cell, which is (IC) read as a counting rule. The remaining $4$ is $A/\SBH$, Bekenstein-Hawking's quarter, which falls on the sphere factor when the sphere is counted at horizon normalisation.

title: The candidate principles and their yields
proof: (P1): $N_{\mathrm{slice}}$ of Proposition \claimref{scrambling.exact-factorisation-thinning}; the slice volume per unit $t$ is $4\pi r_c^2\sqrt{2M/r_c} = 4\pi\sqrt{2M}\,r_c^{3/2}$, proportional to $c_0^{3/2}$ (Lemma \claimref{scrambling.scheme-robustness-cutoff}); the script computes $(c_0/2^{1/3})^{3/2}$ on the prime factorisations, $2^{-1}3^{1} = \tfrac32$ for the proper-time scheme and $2^{1/2}3^{1/4} = 12^{1/4}$ for Kretschmann. (P3): the weights of Fact \claimref{scrambling.imported-collars-coframe-exceptional-set-helicity}, with $(r^{1/2}\sqrt A)^2 = r(1/r - 1) = 1 - r$ evaluated at $r = 0$ by the script; the sphere of radius $r_h$ has $A$ Planck cells, and one per period gives $A$. (P2) is Proposition \claimref{scrambling.per-slice-verification-two-failed-aggregations}.

title: Exactness excludes cutoff dependence
text:
Suppose a calibration principle returns $N_{\mathrm{epoch}} = \SBH = 4\pi M^2$ exactly and its count is a monomial $c\,\pi^p M^m$ in the geometric data of the interior with $c$ rational. Then the count cannot depend on the stretched radius $r_c$: any dependence on $r_c$ through a power $r_c^a$, $a 
eq 0$, carries the scheme constant $c_0^a$, which differs between the three schemes for every real $a 
eq 0$ and, for rational $a$, is irrational for the Kretschmann scheme whenever $a 
otin 6\mathbb{Z}$. The principle must therefore be normalised at a scale the interior fixes without a cutoff. Exactness does not choose that scale: the interior fixes the horizon $r_h = 2M$, at which the sphere carries $A = 4\,\SBH$ cells and the count is $\SBH$ with the residue $	frac14$ on the cells (Proposition \claimref{scrambling.residue-each-convention}(i)), and it fixes equally the rational multiple $r_* = M = r_h/2$, at which the sphere carries $4\pi M^2 = \SBH$ cells and the residue is $1$. Which of the two a principle should mean is not decided here.
proof: $c_0^a$ for the three schemes of \claimref{scrambling.scheme-robustness-cutoff} is $2^{a/3}$, $2^{2a/3}3^{a/6}$, $2^{-a/3}3^{2a/3}$; their ratios $2^{a/3}3^{a/6}$ and $2^{-2a/3}3^{2a/3}$ are not $1$ for real $a \neq 0$, so a count carrying $r_c^a$ takes different values in different schemes, and a scheme-dependent count cannot equal the scheme-independent $\SBH$ in all of them; for rational $a$ the Kretschmann constant $48^{a/6} = 2^{2a/3}\,3^{a/6}$ is rational exactly when both exponents are integers, that is when $a \in 6\mathbb{Z}$, and is otherwise irrational (at $a = 3/2$, for instance, it is $2\cdot 3^{1/4}$). The Schwarzschild interior has one dimensionful parameter, $M$, so a cutoff-free radius is a fixed multiple of $M$; the horizon is the distinguished one, with residue $\tfrac14$ (\claimref{scrambling.residue-each-convention}(i)), and $r_* = M$ is the one at which the residue is $1$, the sphere's cell count there being $\SBH$ itself; the script displays both as arithmetic. The argument excludes the cutoff; it does not rank the two.

title: Pair, mode, qubit: one object
text: The tower's ladder pair $(v_i, w_i)$, the singularity paper's ``fermionic mode'', and the ``one ladder pair per point of the exceptional set'' of Fact \claimref{tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity} are the same object: one creation and one annihilation operator, a two-dimensional state space, one qubit, maximal entropy $\ln 2$ nats. In particular $\Cl(2,4)$ carries exactly two such pairs, its Witt index, and the count of pairs is the count of modes: no factor of two enters between the tower and this paper's count.
proof: The tower's relations \cite[Prop.~4.1]{ButlerT3} (\claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors}) are the CAR of $k$ modes with $v_i$ the creation and $w_i$ the annihilation operator of mode $i$, each mode's algebra $\Mat_2$ with the two-dimensional Fock space $\{|0\rangle, v_i|0\rangle\}$, one qubit per rung \cite[Thm.~4.2]{ButlerT3} (\claimref{tower.fock-module-one-qubit-per-rung}); the singularity paper's per-mode capacity $\ln 2$ is the maximal entropy of that two-state system; the corank statement counts these pairs. The script realises two pairs in $\Cl(2,4)$ as $v_i = \tfrac12(e_a + e_b)$, $w_i = \tfrac12(e_a - e_b)$ on two orthogonal hyperbolic planes and checks all ten anticommutation relations exactly, the CAR of a Witt basis (\claimref{std-algebra.witt-basis-car}); that no third pair exists is the capacity theorem \cite[Thm.~4.3]{ButlerT3} (\claimref{tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity}).

title: The residue in each convention
proof: (i) and (ii) are $N_{\mathrm{epoch}}/A$ with $N_{\mathrm{epoch}}$ read off Corollary \claimref{scrambling.integer-holographic-form-identification}(2) in each convention: $N_{\mathrm{epoch}} = \SBH = 4\pi M^2$ in the 1-nat convention and $N_{\mathrm{epoch}} = \SBH/\ln 2$ in the capacity convention (the $\ln 2$ of Remark \claimref{note.scrambling.density-factor-stated-full}), divided by $A = 16\pi M^2$; the script performs them as exact monomials in $\pi$ and $M$ with $\ln 2$ a formal indeterminate. (iii): the maximal entropy of a two-dimensional state space is $\ln 2$, the entropy of the maximally mixed state, and $\ln 2 < 1$; the singularity paper already compares $C = N\ln 2$ with $\SBH$ for this reason \cite[Prop.~10.7]{ButlerT5} (\claimref{singularity.area-law-test}), and Remark \claimref{note.scrambling.density-factor-stated-full} records the factor. (iv) is a reading of the lift of \claimref{scrambling.imported-collars-coframe-exceptional-set-helicity} at the level of its channel identification, its modelling step: the homogeneities $-2s - 2$ at $s = \pm 1, \pm 2$ are $-4, 0, -6, +2$, pairwise distinct, so no single channel contains both helicities; the script checks the table.

title: No recount reaches the quarter
text: Let a counting rule assign to the exceptional set a tally that is a rational number of modes per cell, with cells whose areas are rational multiples of integer powers of $\pi$ in Planck units, over a rational number of ticks per modular period. Then its residue $\kappa_c$ is a rational multiple of an integer power of $\pi$, $\kappa_c = q\pi^k$ with $q \in \mathbb{Q}$ and $k \in \mathbb{Z}$. In the capacity convention the target is $\kappa_c = 1/(4\ln 2)$; equality would require $\pi^k\ln 2 \in \mathbb{Q}$, which is false for $k = 0$, $\ln 2$ being transcendental \cite[Thm.~1.4]{Baker1975}, so no rule with $k = 0$ reaches the target; for $k \neq 0$ it would contradict the expected algebraic independence of $\pi$ and $\ln 2$, which is not a theorem, so the exclusion of rules with $k \neq 0$ is conditional on that independence. In the 1-nat convention the target $\kappa_c = \tfrac14$ is rational, and the natural rules of Proposition \claimref{scrambling.candidate-principles-their-yields} return $\kappa_c = 4\pi$ (P1), $\kappa_c = 1$ (P3) and a broken scaling (P2), none of them $\tfrac14$.
proof: A product and quotient of rational multiples of integer powers of $\pi$ is one, which is the closure the script checks on the rule's three factors. For the capacity target of \claimref{scrambling.residue-each-convention}(ii), $1/(4\ln 2) = q\pi^k$ with $q$ rational gives $\pi^k\ln 2 = 1/(4q)$ rational; at $k = 0$ this says $\ln 2$ is rational, contradicting its transcendence (Hermite-Lindemann, an import, not scripted). The residues of the natural rules are Proposition \claimref{scrambling.candidate-principles-their-yields}'s yields divided by $A$: $16\pi\,\SBH/A = 4\pi$ and $A/A = 1$.

title: The prediction, restated
text:
Propositions \claimref{scrambling.exact-factorisation-thinning} to \claimref{scrambling.no-recount-reaches-quarter} reduce the calibration to the form
\[
N_{\mathrm{epoch}} \;=\; \kappa_c \times (\text{horizon-normalised sphere cells}) \times (\text{one tick per modular period}),
\]
with the normalisation narrowed to two cutoff-free scales by exactness ($r_h$, or $r_* = M$, Proposition \claimref{scrambling.exactness-excludes-cutoff-dependence}), one tick per period being (IC) read as a counting rule, and $\kappa_c$ the residue. The residue is not an artefact of the counting conventions: the chain from tower to count carries no hidden factor of two (Proposition \claimref{scrambling.pair-mode-qubit-one-object}); the helicity clause is closed at the tier of the lift's modelling joint J3 (Proposition \claimref{scrambling.residue-each-convention}(iv), Fact \claimref{scrambling.imported-collars-coframe-exceptional-set-helicity}), not at theorem tier; and in the one convention with physical content the residue is $1/(4\ln 2)$, which no recount of the exceptional set with a rational residue ($k = 0$) produces, and, conditionally on the expected algebraic independence of $\pi$ and $\ln 2$, no recount with $k \neq 0$ either (Proposition \claimref{scrambling.no-recount-reaches-quarter}). The prediction's declared form is therefore: \emph{the boundary mode space registers one mode per Bekenstein-Mukhanov area quantum of horizon per modular period}, $\nu = 1/(16\pi\ln 2)$ in the capacity convention, and deriving that is equivalent to deriving Bekenstein-Hawking's quarter. Arithmetically $\kappa_c = \tfrac14$ in the 1-nat convention is horizon normalisation replaced by normalisation at $r_* = r_h/2 = M$, since $4\pi M^2 = \SBH$; whether that radius means anything is not decided here. The $16\pi$ of Theorem \claimref{scrambling.epoch-modular-period-two-unknowns-become} stands as the convention-dependent form of the same statement.

title: The transverse sphere from the boundary modes
The transverse sphere from the boundary modes
text: The count of the section ``The count'' used the metric slice geometry. This section derives the transverse angular geometry from the correlation structure itself, completing a sequence whose first two steps are standard modular theory, and then runs the quantitative checks: one exact agreement, and two instructive failures.

title: Imported: time and the plane from modular data
text: The modular flow of a wedge algebra in the vacuum implements the boost: the timelike direction is recoverable from modular data (Bisognano-Wichmann). One half-sided modular inclusion recovers the two-dimensional conformal structure (Wiesbrock). \emph{Provenance:} \cite{BisognanoWichmann1976} (the duality theorem) and \cite{Wiesbrock1993} (the main theorem); both at assembly level for the present use.
provenance: J. J. Bisognano and E. H. Wichmann, On the duality condition for quantum fields, J. Math. Phys. 17 (1976), 303--321.; H.-W. Wiesbrock, Half-sided modular inclusions of von Neumann algebras, Commun. Math. Phys. 157 (1993), 83--92.

title: The boundary mode space as matrix
text: Let the boundary mode space carry $n$ completed pairs, $n$ counted after the completion's doubling (each mode with its adjoined partner). The gauge-invariant bilinears $E_{ij} := \psi_i^\dagger \psi_j$ satisfy $[E_{ij}, E_{kl}] = \delta_{jk}E_{il} - \delta_{li}E_{kj}$ (the $\mathfrak{gl}(n)$ relations, an instance of the CAR bilinear commutator), preserve the one-particle subspace, and restrict on it to the full matrix algebra: $E_{ij}|_{\text{one-particle}} = $ the matrix unit $e_{ij}$, so the associative algebra they generate restricts onto $\Mat_n$. The doubling the completion forces is exactly what turns a tower of modes into a matrix; and matrices can be spheres.
proof: The commutator identity is the bilinear computation used already in \cite[Prop.~6.1]{ButlerT7} (there for the currents; here for general index pairs): $[\psi_i^\dagger\psi_j, \psi_k^\dagger\psi_l] = \delta_{jk}\psi_i^\dagger\psi_l - \delta_{li}\psi_k^\dagger\psi_j$ from the CAR (\claimref{std-algebra.witt-basis-car}). Each $E_{ij}$ maps the one-particle subspace $\operatorname{span}\{\psi_k^\dagger|0\rangle\}$ to itself, acting as $e_{ij}$ ($E_{ij}\psi_k^\dagger|0\rangle = \delta_{jk}\psi_i^\dagger|0\rangle$); the matrix units generate $\Mat_n$, so the restriction map is onto. The doubling is what supplies the complex structure: each real mode with its adjoined partner supplies the complex $\psi_i, \psi_i^\dagger$ from which the gauge-invariant $E_{ij}$ are built; real Clifford directions alone give the orthogonal bilinears, and it is the pairing that produces $\mathfrak{gl}(n)$. The script checks the commutator table and the one-particle action exactly on a five-mode instance.

title: Imported: Kostant, Madore, and the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ partition data
text: (i) Embeddings of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ into $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ are classified, up to conjugation, by the partition of $n$ given by the restriction of the defining representation; the \emph{principal} embedding is the one with a single part (the irreducible $n$-dimensional representation), and it is essentially unique. (ii) For the principal embedding the adjoint decomposition of $\Mat_n$ is multiplicity-free: $\Mat_n \cong \bigoplus_{\ell=0}^{n-1}(2\ell + 1)$, one spin-$\ell$ multiplet for each $\ell < n$ (Kostant). (iii) $\Mat_n$ with this $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ structure is Madore's fuzzy sphere, whose large-$n$ limit is the round $S^2$ \cite{Madore1992}, radius excluded: the radius is scale. \emph{Provenance:} \cite{Kostant1959} (the principal three-dimensional subgroup and the multiplicity-free adjoint decomposition) and \cite{Madore1992} (the fuzzy sphere and its large-$n$ limit); the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ classification is classical representation theory.

title: Principality from indifference: the sphere
text: Under Principle \claimref{scrambling.indifference-structural-premise-series}, the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ structure carried by the matrix algebra of the boundary modes (Proposition \claimref{scrambling.boundary-mode-space-matrix}) is the principal embedding, uniquely: a non-principal embedding decomposes the $n$ modes into invariant blocks, a partition whose sizes and assignments nothing in the framework causes (Fact \claimref{scrambling.imported-kostant-madore-partition-data}(i)), and indifference forbids exactly such uncaused data; the principal embedding is the unique one carrying no partition data, its internal distinctions forced by the algebra once conjugation-gauge is fixed. The conclusion is conditional on Principle \claimref{scrambling.indifference-structural-premise-series} wherever this theorem is cited.

title: The per-slice verification, and the two failed aggregations
text:
Let $n$ be the linear size of the slice's matrix algebra. Then:

title: Scrambling, and the return delay
text: T5's eviction dynamics is a rate model, and its instant information return was flagged there as the rate model's artefact. This section supplies the internal timescales of the boundary modes at the same declared tier: a rate model whose clock, unlike its couplings, is a theorem.

title: The spreading law, and the chaos bound met, not saturated
text:
Three framework-internal facts fix the window's internal dynamics. First, the intrinsic flows of a Clifford boundary-mode algebra are bivector-generated, quadratic in the pair operators (Lemma \claimref{scrambling.clock-inventory-boundary-modes}(i)). Second, the distinguished bivector flow is the boost (Fact \claimref{scrambling.imported-modes-modular-inventory}). Third, the boost is the translation clock of the window itself: the Killing flow that displaces modes along the window is the boost at rate $\kappa$, with the accrual rate of Theorem \claimref{scrambling.mode-count}. Boost-hyperbolic one-body dynamics expands operator amplitudes as $e^{\kappa t}$, so support deposited on a single mode spans the $N$-mode window at
\[
t_* \;=\; \kappa^{-1}\ln N \;=\; \frac{\beta}{2\pi}\,\ln S :
\]
the fast-scrambling law, with the logarithm the signature of hyperbolic dynamics rather than an assumption. Every intrinsic clock it has runs at the modular rate, and the expansion rate is exactly $2\pi T$: the boost group's support-dilation rate equals its KMS rate, $\kappa\beta = 2\pi$, which holds under (N$_{+}$) (\claimref{synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state}). The real-time Lyapunov exponent of this quasi-free dynamics is $0$: the one unitary group that dilates the support has bounded anticommutators on linear elements (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boost-evolution-on-generators-is-one-unitary-group}). So the Maldacena-Shenker-Stanford chaos bound is met, not saturated. \emph{Tier, declared:} what is derived is the free-fermion operator-spreading timescale under a generic quadratic coupling, in the rate-model normalisation; genuine chaotic saturation beyond free-fermion spreading is open, and is named as such in the section ``Scope, and successor problems''.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{The derivation, step by step.} The inventory clauses are Lemma \claimref{scrambling.clock-inventory-boundary-modes} (proved) and its import (Fact \claimref{scrambling.imported-modes-modular-inventory}). The expansion computation: a quadratic generator containing the boost scales ladder operators by $e^{\pm\kappa t}$ (Fact \claimref{scrambling.imported-modes-modular-inventory}'s weight clause, exponentiated), so under a generic quadratic coupling the amplitude reaching a mode at mode distance $d$ grows as $e^{\kappa t}$ against an initial suppression of order $1/N$; support spans all the boundary modes when $e^{\kappa t} \sim N$, i.e.\ at $t_* = \kappa^{-1}\ln N$, and $N \sim S$ over an epoch of order $M$ (Proposition \claimref{scrambling.area-law-test}). The identification $\kappa^{-1} = \beta/2\pi$ is arithmetic ($\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$), checked by the script along with the Schwarzschild value $\beta/2\pi = 4M$. The MSS statement that no system exceeds the growth rate $2\pi T$ is the point of contact \cite{MSS2016}: the rate $\kappa$ at which support dilates is one group's rate set against its own KMS period $2\pi/\kappa$, while the out-of-time-order growth that the bound limits is absent from the quasi-free dynamics, so the bound is met and not saturated.
proof: Follows from \claimref{scrambling.clock-inventory-boundary-modes}, \claimref{scrambling.imported-modes-modular-inventory}, \claimref{scrambling.mode-count} and \claimref{scrambling.area-law-test}, as the source states.

title: The return delay: the scrambling log recovered
text:
In the rate model, deposited information cannot return before the dwell time of the window (the epoch of the section ``The epoch is the modular period'', the correct power of $M$); and charging the window-internal re-encoding at the framework's causal rate (one pairwise operation per boost e-fold $\kappa^{-1}$ per mode, spreading epidemically over the $N \sim S$ modes) requires of order $\ln S$ rounds of duration $\beta/2\pi$, giving a return delay
\[
T_{\mathrm{return}} \;\approx\; \frac{\beta}{2\pi}\,\ln S \;=\; 4M\,\ln S :
\]
the fast-scrambling time \cite{HaydenPreskill2007, SekinoSusskind2008}, recovered from the framework's own clock. This removes the instant-return artefact of T5's rate model; the first-principles account of the spreading exponent is Assembly \claimref{scrambling.spreading-law-chaos-bound-saturated}, and genuine chaotic dynamics beyond it remains open.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{The derivation, step by step.} The dwell floor is the epoch (Theorem \claimref{scrambling.epoch-modular-period-two-unknowns-become}, conditional on (IC)); the epidemic count is the standard doubling estimate, $\log_2 S$ rounds to reach $S$ modes from one, each round one causal step of the window's clock, the $\ln 2$ absorbed into the displayed approximation; the clock and its rate are the theorems cited. The coefficient $4M$ is exact arithmetic from $\beta = 8\pi M$, script-checked.

text:

title: The residue, the s-wave weights and the boundary-mode prediction
text: The calibration residue was not derived (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy}). Under the area-law hypothesis it is the reciprocal of four times the counted modes' mean thermal entropy, so the registered value $\kappa_{c} = 1/(4\ln 2)$ of Prediction \claimref{pred.boundary-mode-density} is the case in which every counted mode has zero Killing weight. Counting arrays gives $0.3470$ against $0.3607$, about four per cent low; counting every mode drives the residue up without bound; counting only the zero-weight modes leaves $0.0272$ nats per array outside the area law. title: The helicity lift, with its joints itemised
text:
Helicity is not additional structure imported into the framework: it is the eigenvalue of the distinguished $\mathfrak{u}(1)$ charge of the completion's conformal storey (the twistor storey: $\Cl(2,4)$ with its conformal spinor space $\CS$), and the four-dimensional mode space of each massless species has a canonical place in it. The joints, each with its provenance:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (\emph{Joint J1: the transform, classical.}) By Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-penrose-transform}, the helicity-$s$ mode space is the cohomology at homogeneity $-2s-2$; photon kinematics are at homogeneities $-4$ and $0$ ($s = \pm1$), graviton kinematics at $-6$ and $+2$ ($s = \pm2$).
\item (\emph{Joint J2: the charge, proved in the series.}) The ordering shift is proved in the correspondence paper (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-twistor-storey-ordering-shift}), and Proposition \claimref{hawking.homogeneity-ordering-shift} derives the homogeneity $-2s-2$ from it: the classification parameter of Joint J1 is an internal charge of the completion, so the helicity ladder is part of the ascended kinematics rather than a phenomenological label.
\item (\emph{Joint J3: the reduction, modelling.}) The current boson of the s-wave theory (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-s-wave-bosonic-sector}) is the s-wave reduction of each such four-dimensional field, and the lift from the boundary modes to the field is the standard partial-wave reconstruction, each helicity sector identified through the transform of Joint J1: the near-horizon reduction of field theory on the Schwarzschild exterior identifies each $(\omega, \ell, m, s)$ channel with a two-dimensional mode, which is where Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.continuum-mode-space}'s modelling input enters, flagged as such in Remark \claimref{note.hawking.which-dynamics-what-level}.
\end{enumerate}
The composite statement is the conjunction of the three joints with the provenance displayed: J1 is classical, J2 is Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-twistor-storey-ordering-shift} together with Proposition \claimref{hawking.homogeneity-ordering-shift}, and J3 is the one modelling joint. The homogeneity table is checked by the script.

title: The homogeneity $-2s-2$ is the ordering shift
text:
On functions on the conformal spinor space $\CS$ (twistor functions), realise the palatial relation of Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-twistor-storey-ordering-shift} by $\bar Z_\nu = -\hbar\,\partial/\partial Z^\nu$ (the realisation with the palatial sign $[Z^\mu, \bar Z_\nu] = +\hbar\,\delta^\mu_\nu$), let $\Upsilon := Z^\mu \partial_\mu$ be the homogeneity (Euler) operator, its eigenvalue written $\mathsf{h}$ in sans serif to keep it clear of the one-particle Hamiltonian $h$, and let the helicity operator be one half the distinguished charge, $\mathsf{s} := \tfrac12\, q(\id)$, the standard helicity operator on $\CS$ (twistor helicity) \cite{Penrose1969, EPW1981} in the symmetric ordering that Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-twistor-storey-ordering-shift} forces storey-wide. Then, as an operator identity,
\[
q(\id) \;=\; -\hbar\,(\Upsilon + 2),
\]
so a function on $\CS$ homogeneous of degree $\mathsf{h}$ is an eigenfunction of $\mathsf{s}$ with eigenvalue $s\hbar$ if and only if
\[
\mathsf{h} \;=\; -2s - 2.
\]
The $-2$ is exactly the ordering shift: without the symmetric-ordering shift of $-\hbar/2$ per complex dimension (over the complex unit $I_6$) the offset would vanish. Combined with Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-penrose-transform}, the classification parameter of the Penrose transform is the completion's own $\mathfrak{u}(1)$ charge, its offset supplied by the ordering. The computation is not new to the series: it appears, without being stated as a result, inside the proof of \cite[Thm.~5.7]{ButlerT9}, where T9's script also checks it; what this proposition adds is the statement at result level, in the transform's context, discharging the homogeneity half of the successor problem T9 assigns to this paper (the transform itself stays open).

title: Imported: the Penrose transform

title: Imported: quasi-free states of the CAR algebra
text: For every operator $A$ on $\ell^2(J)$ with $0 \le A \le 1$ (the \emph{symbol}) there is a unique gauge-invariant state $\omega_A$ on $\mathfrak{A}$ with two-point function $\omega_A(a^\dagger(f)\,a(g)) = \ip{g}{Af}$ and all higher truncated functions zero (Wick determinants). More generally, a quasi-free state (all truncated functions beyond second order vanishing) is determined by its full two-point data, the symbol together with the pairing $P(f, g) := \omega(a^\dagger(f)\,a^\dagger(g))$, and gauge invariance is exactly $P = 0$. On a finite window with diagonal symbol this is the explicit product state $\bigotimes_j \rho_j$, $\rho_j = \mathrm{diag}(1 - n_j,\, n_j)$ in the occupation basis, which the script realises exactly. \emph{Provenance:} Araki \cite{Araki1971}; \cite[\S 5.2]{BratteliRobinson1997}.

title: The interior connection, exactly
text:

\[
\Omega(e_1) = -\sigma_1 B_1, \qquad
\Omega(e_2) = -\sigma_2 B_2, \qquad
\Omega(e_3) = -\sigma_3 B_3 + \frac{\cot\theta}{r}\,R_{23},

title: Kasner form of the interior
text:
In the interior, with $A(r) := 2M/r - 1 > 0$, the Schwarzschild gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), taken in a synchronous position gauge, has derived metric of diagonal form
\[
ds^2 \;=\; d\tau^2 - A\,dt^2 - r^2\,d\Omega^2,
\qquad
\tau(r) \;=\; \int_0^r A(u)^{-1/2}\,du ,
\]
where $\tau$ is proper time along the radial timelike worldlines ruling the interior, whose velocity $\hb^{-1}(x')$ is $D$-parallel (the geodesics of the derived metric), normalised so that the singularity is $\tau = 0$. In units $2M = 1$,
\[
\tau(r) \;=\; \tfrac23\, r^{3/2}\bigl(1 + \tfrac{3}{10}\,r + O(r^2)\bigr),
\qquad
r \;=\; R\,\bigl(1 - \tfrac15 R + O(R^2)\bigr), \quad R := (3\tau/2)^{2/3},
\]
and the scale factors obey $\sqrt{A} \propto \tau^{-1/3}$ and $r \propto \tau^{2/3}$ to leading order: the Kasner exponents of the approach are
\[
(p_1, p_2, p_3) \;=\; \bigl(-\tfrac13,\ \tfrac23,\ \tfrac23\bigr),
\qquad
p_1 + p_2 + p_3 \;=\; 1, \qquad p_1^2 + p_2^2 + p_3^2 \;=\; 1 .
\]

title: The area-law test
text:
Assume (C1)-(C3), write $N_{\mathrm{6a}} = (dN_{\mathrm{6a}}/dt)\,\Delta t$ for the mode count of the counted epoch, and let $C := N_{\mathrm{6a}}\ln 2$ be its boundary-mode capacity in nats, $\ln 2$ per fermionic mode. Then, at leading order in $M$, $C = S_{\mathrm{BH}} = 4\pi M^2$ if and only if $
u\,\Delta t = M/(2\ln 2)$: the capacity matches the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy \cite{Bekenstein1973, Hawking1975}, the coefficient calibrated by $
u\,\Delta t$ rather than predicted (the closing paragraph of this section quantifies the conventions), exactly when the counted epoch is of order one Schwarzschild time, which is what (C3) supplies via Lemma \claimref{singularity.causal-epoch-computed-exactly}, the $\ln 2$ being absorbed into the order-one calibration of $
u\,\Delta t$. It is the capacity, not the bare count, that premise (C) and Fact \claimref{singularity.assembled-page-curve-up-typicality} compare with $S_{\mathrm{BH}}$; the count itself then reads $N_{\mathrm{6a}} = S_{\mathrm{BH}}/\ln 2$. Counting over the hole's whole lifetime instead gives $N_{\mathrm{6a}} \sim M^4$, which shares with the interior-volume growth of Christodoulou-Rovelli \cite{CR2015} the linearity in advanced time and the unresolved tension with the constancy of the horizon entropy, though not the mass scaling: their $dV/dv \propto M^{2}$ gives $V \sim M^{5}$ over the lifetime, while $dN_{\mathrm{6a}}/dt \propto M$ gives $M^{4}$ here.

title: The causal epoch, computed exactly
text:
For the Schwarzschild gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), along the rain worldlines of the interior, the radial infall worldlines with unit energy at infinity whose velocity $\hb^{-1}(x')$ is $D$-parallel and which are the worldlines of the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand frame of the section ``Step 1: locate the failure'' (velocity $e_t$ in the gauge $\hb = 1 - \beta P$), $|dt/dr| = \sqrt{r/2M}\;r/(2M - r)$ in static Killing time $t$, so the span of Killing time between crossing $r = 2M(1 - \varepsilon)$ and reaching the singular locus $r = 0$ is
\[
\Delta t(\varepsilon) \;=\; \int_0^{2M(1-\varepsilon)} \sqrt{\frac{r}{2M}}\,\frac{r\,dr}{2M - r}
\;=\; 4M\Bigl(\tfrac12\ln\frac{1+u}{1-u} - u - \tfrac{u^{3}}{3}\Bigr)\Big|_{u = \sqrt{1-\varepsilon}}
\;=\; 2M\Bigl(\ln\tfrac{1}{\varepsilon} - \tfrac83 + 2\ln 2\Bigr) + O(\varepsilon) :
\]
of order $M$ for any fixed regulator $\varepsilon$, with only logarithmic sensitivity to the horizon-crossing cutoff, the coefficient $2M$ of the logarithm being independent of the worldline's energy. The informal estimate ``$\Delta t \sim M$ up to a logarithm'' is exactly this statement, with the logarithm identified.

using $r_c^{3} = 2M$: the cutoff radius conspires with the anisotropic stretch to leave \emph{linear} mass dependence at leading order, special to this cutoff (a mass-independent cutoff radius gives $M^{1/2}$ and can never reach the area law). With $\nu$ fermionic modes per Planck cell, and writing $N_{\mathrm{6a}}$ for the number of boundary modes (the notation Steps 6b and Fact \claimref{singularity.assembled-page-curve-up-typicality} use for this section's count),
\[

\]
the stretched singularity registers $\nu$ modes per Hawking period up to the correction factor $\sqrt{1 - r_c/2M}$, which tends to $1$ as $M \to \infty$ in Planck units ($r_c/2M = (2M)^{-2/3}$). It keeps time with the horizon's own clock.

title: Answers to the iteration question
text:
Let $(M, G)$ be a tame corank-one degeneration in the sense of \cite[Hyp.~2.1]{ButlerT4}, with trivial radical line bundle and compact wall as in Fact \claimref{tower.wall-package}, presenting the transport demand of the series' geometric setting.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Where ascent is forced.} On the physical closure, one ascent completes the description: by Fact \claimref{tower.wall-package} the one-sided completion is nondegenerate up to and including the wall and the transported reciprocal divides totally there; nothing on the physical side demands a second rung. Beyond the physical region, the demand repeats: by Fact \claimref{tower.wall-package} the degeneration relocates to a tame shadow wall, and the infinite wall sequence carries exactly one rung of this paper's tower per wall, displaced successively away from the physical region.
\item \emph{Why the clock never ticks.} Theorem \claimref{tower.rigidity-clock-frozen}: the tower is Morita-stationary from its first step, and the mod-8 structure classifies the eight parallel towers, not stages of one.
\item \emph{What the limit is.} Theorems \claimref{tower.algebraic-limit-even-charge} and \claimref{tower.car-limit-even-charge}: for even transport charge, the ground algebra tensored with the free fermionic field algebra, the modes being the transported null pairs themselves.
\end{enumerate}
The depth of the hierarchy, on this account: one forced conformal ascent, plus a fermionic ladder of capacity, one qubit per rung.

title: Fock module; one qubit per rung
text: Let $W_k := \operatorname{span}\{v_1, \dots, v_k\}$, a maximal isotropic subspace of $H_1 \perp \cdots \perp H_k$. The Chevalley action ($v_j$ by wedge, $w_j$ by contraction against the pairing) makes the exterior algebra $\Lambda^\bullet W_k$, of dimension $2^k$, an irreducible module over $B_k \cong \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$, with the vacuum $1 \in \Lambda^0$ annihilated by every $w_j$ and cyclic for the $v_j$. Each rung doubles the module: $\Lambda^\bullet W_{k+1} = \Lambda^\bullet W_k \otimes \Lambda^\bullet \R v_{k+1}$, one qubit per rung.

\[
v_i v_j + v_j v_i = 0, \qquad w_i w_j + w_j w_i = 0, \qquad v_i w_j + w_j v_i = \delta_{ij}\,,
\]
for all $1 \leq i, j \leq k$: a system of $k$ fermionic modes, with no normal-ordering, no completion, and no representation chosen. Adding a rung adds one mode and touches none of the existing relations.

title: Witt index is quantum capacity
text: For any nondegenerate real quadratic space $(V, Q)$, the maximal number of pairwise-anticommuting fermionic mode pairs realisable by \emph{vectors} of $\Cl(V, Q)$ (families $(a_i, b_i)$ of vectors satisfying the displayed CAR of Proposition \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors}) is exactly the Witt index $\min(p,q)$ of $Q$. Along the tower the Witt index is $\min(p,q) + k$: each rung raises the algebra's mode capacity by exactly one, and by no more.
